caption:
You prompt AI the way Maa writes recipes: “a pinch of this, cook till done”.

That works for family, because they have eaten the dish a hundred times. AI has never eaten at your table. It is a stranger in your kitchen.

So I tested it. Same model, same day, each prompt run twice. The test scenario: dinner for 2 vegetarians, no oven. Prompt 1 was “Give me a healthy dinner recipe”. Both times it gave lemon chicken with roasted vegetables and quinoa, oven at 220°C. That is a fair answer. It had no way to know the dinner was vegetarian, or that the test kitchen had no oven. One run even ended: “If you tell me your calorie or protein target, or what's in your fridge, I can tailor it.”

Prompt 2 was a recipe card with six labelled lines. Both times it gave a palak paneer moong dal built from what the card listed, with grams and minutes in the steps, in about 25 to 27 minutes. It put the protein at about 34 g per serving. That number is the AI's own estimate, not verified nutrition. Each run ended with one question to make the dish better. This was a test prompt, not a cooked meal.

The six lines:
Serves: who it is for
Ingredients: what you have
Method: the shape of the answer you want
Tastes like: one example
Don't: your limits
Taste and adjust: ask it to check its own work and ask you one question

This is not a magic prompt. It is what you would tell any stranger cooking in your kitchen. Try the same six lines on an email or a study plan.
